feedback.problem:
Using the fact that $-{210}^{∘}={30}^{∘}-{240}^{∘},$
calculate the **exact** value of $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-{210}^{∘}).$

$\operatorname{cos}⁡(-{210}^{∘})=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for cosine with $x={30}^{∘}$ and $y={240}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-{210}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({30}^{∘}-{240}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({30}^{∘})\operatorname{cos}⁡({240}^{∘})+\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘})\operatorname{sin}⁡({240}^{∘}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
